scenes.title: Virtual Environments & Dependency Management
scenes.narration: A virtual environment gives each project its own isolated set of Python packages, so projects never interfere with one another.

scenes.title: Why Isolate
bullets: Different projects often need different, conflicting versions of the same library.
Isolation keeps your system Python clean and untouched.
Pinned dependencies make your environment reproducible for teammates and servers.
scenes.narration: One project might need an old version of a library while another needs the newest, and only isolation lets both coexist. A virtual environment also shields your global Python installation from being polluted by project-specific packages. And by pinning exactly which versions you use, anyone can rebuild the identical environment on another machine.

scenes.title: The Environment Workflow
scenes.narration: You start by creating a fresh environment for the project, then activate it so pip installs go into that sandbox. After adding the packages you need, you freeze them to a requirements file for reproducibility. When you switch projects, you deactivate to step back out.

scenes.title: venv in Practice
scenes.code:
python3 -m venv venv         # create environment
source venv/bin/activate     # activate it
pip install pandas requests  # install packages
pip freeze > requirements.txt
deactivate                   # exit the env
scenes.narration: The venv module creates a self-contained environment in a local folder. Sourcing its activate script switches your shell to use it, which you can confirm by the prompt changing. From there pip installs land inside the environment, and pip freeze captures the exact versions into requirements.txt. Running deactivate returns you to the system Python.

scenes.text: One environment per project, always tracked with requirements.txt — never install project packages into your global Python.
scenes.narration: Give every project its own environment and commit a requirements file alongside the code. Keeping the global Python pristine saves you from countless version conflicts down the road.
